alt: Headline: A $180,000 year comes down to two conversations a day.
Table working backward from $180,000 GCI to 20 closings, 40 appointments, 400 conversations, about 8 a week and about 2 a day.
The Break It Down page from the planner showing the conversation math worksheet.
Find your daily number. The 2027 Real Estate Business Planning Guide and Planner.
caption:
Meet Taylor. Taylor wants a $180,000 year.

$180,000 ÷ $9,000 average commission = 20 closings
20 closings at a 50% close rate = 40 appointments
40 appointments at a 10% conversion = 400 conversations
400 conversations over 48 working weeks = about 8 a week
That's about 2 real conversations a day.

Your numbers will be different. The planner walks you through the same math with yours, step by step.

What's your daily number? Save this for your planning session.

alt: A filled-in Weekly CEO Meeting spread showing wins, lessons, a daily habit scorecard, active deals and follow-ups.
caption:
Sunday night is when the week gets decided.

The Weekly CEO Meeting is a two-page check-in with yourself:
• Look back: wins, what worked, what didn't
• Score your daily habits against your goal
• Check every active deal and its next step
• List who you'll follow up with and why
• Pick your top three for next week

About 30 minutes. Every week. It's the habit that keeps the plan alive.

alt: Your people are your pipeline. 1 in 24 homeowners moves in a given year. 66% of sellers hire an agent they were referred to or worked with before. 43% of buyers found their agent through a friend, neighbor or relative.
caption:
Homeowners are moving less than ever, about 1 in 24 a year.

That makes every relationship in your database worth more, not less. Two out of three sellers hire someone they were referred to or have worked with before.

Your people are your pipeline. Who are you calling this week?

Sources: U.S. Census Bureau CPS (2023); NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers.

alt: Two planner pages, Life Aspirations and Put a Price on It, under the headline Plan your life first, then put a price on it.
caption:
Most business plans start with a sales goal. This one starts with your life.

First you write down what you want this year: family, adventure, giving back, career. Then you put a price on it, add taxes and your split, and land on a target that actually means something to you.

A number with a reason behind it is a lot easier to chase.

alt: A filled-in My Week and My People spread: three weekly goals, a day-by-day plan, and a list of contacts with why and how to reach out.
caption:
Who are you talking to this week?

Every week in the planner includes a My People page with room for up to 20 names, why you're reaching out and how (call, text, note, visit). Check them off as you go.

Small list. Every week. That's how a database turns into a business.

alt: The goodwill gap: 91% of buyers would use their agent again or recommend them, but only 15% actually used an agent they'd worked with before.
caption:
91% of buyers say they'd use their agent again or recommend them.
Only 15% actually used an agent they'd worked with before.

That gap is goodwill most agents never collect. Staying in touch is how you close it.

Source: NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers.
